 India’s SAFF campaign hit by player exodus 
 India’s SAFF campaign hit by player exodus 
 Marcus Mergulhao / TNN / Nov 08, 2026, 00:00 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Four of coach Moosa’s starters against Pakistan will no longer have a role to play at the SAFF Championship Panaji: Naushad Moosa’s woes at the SAFF Championship are unending. The India coach had 17 players to choose from for the opener against Pakistan. But while he expected 10 new players to join and strengthen his hands in Dhaka after their club engagements in the Indian Super League (ISL), he has had to contend with injuries, key players returning home, and three others being summoned for friendlies against New Zealand. According to sources, the All India Football Federation (AIFF) had an understanding with Mumbai City that the club would release three players -- Farukh Choudhary, Noufal PN and Valpuia – for international duty outside the window but would return to Mumbai after the opener against Pakistan. “We thought three players returning from the camp wouldn’t disturb the equation since there would still be 25 players available,” said a team source. Unfortunately for Moosa, Ronney Wilson (FC Goa) and Suresh Singh (Bengaluru FC) picked up injuries during club games. Injuries to senior team regulars Anwar Ali, Apuia and Mohammed Sanan then prompted senior team coach Khalid Jamil to replace them with Muhammad Suhail, Bijoy Varghese and Liston Colaco, all of whom were previously marked for SAFF duty. “We are left with only 20 players but can still put up a competitive squad at SAFF Championship,” said another official. “Prior to the clash against Pakistan, nobody really gave India a chance, but the team proved that it can be more than a handful.” Four of Moosa’s starters against Pakistan will no longer have a role to play at the SAFF Championship. The organisers allowed teams to register a maximum of 28 players, instead of the regular 23, since the tournament was played outside the FIFA international window. As per tournament regulations, no replacements are allowed. India kickstarted their campaign with a 3-2 win against Pakistan. Moosa's side took control with three first-half goals, but a late lapse in concentration allowed their opponents to score twice in stoppage time. “We played some very good football, particularly in the first half,” said Moosa. “We were organised, created good opportunities, and showed a good understanding of what we wanted to achieve both in and out of possession. However, the last few minutes were not what we expected. “At this level, concentration, game management and maintaining our discipline are extremely important until the final whistle. We will analyse those moments, but I don’t want to take away from the overall effort and performance of the players. There are positives to build on, along with lessons we must learn.” India play their final group B fixture against Maldives on Nov 11. Two of the three teams in the group qualify for the semifinals.
